strategy.summary: Reproduce the strict-vs-nonstrict stopping check in enet_coordinate_descent_gram (_cd_fast.pyx). The buggy revision uses gap < tol and d_w_max/w_max < d_w_tol; the fix uses <=. The most direct transition test is test_lasso_zero, where y and X are all zero so the scaled tolerance is exactly 0.0 and the duality gap is exactly 0.0. On the buggy build 0.0 < 0.0 is false, so a ConvergenceWarning is raised, and the PR removed the ignore_warnings wrapper around that call. On the fixed build 0.0 <= 0.0 is true and no warning is raised.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy era ceiling 2.3 is an era-inferred constraint (dependency_constraints, kind explicit but era_ceiling derived from PR date 2025-08-12), not a hard documented pin; relied on only to keep the NumPy ABI matching the Cython build
SciPy era ceiling 1.15 is era-inferred in the same way; the documented constraint is only the >= |SciPyMinVersion| placeholder
joblib and threadpoolctl are documented but numerically irrelevant, so they are unpinned

strategy.reproducing_test: sklearn/linear_model/tests/test_coordinate_descent.py::test_lasso_zero (the warning-suppression wrapper was removed by the PR). Secondary check: sklearn/linear_model/tests/test_coordinate_descent.py::test_enet_coordinate_descent, which the PR rewrote with alpha=1e-10, warm_start and max_iter=1.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (3c74809cb3ef), test_lasso_zero fails: Lasso(alpha=0.1).fit on X=[[0],[0],[0]], y=[0,0,0] emits a ConvergenceWarning because gap 0.0 is not strictly less than tol-scaled 0.0, so the explicit ConvergenceWarning-as-error turns this into a test failure. On the fixed revision, the same test passes because 0.0 <= 0.0 terminates the loop with no warning.
strategy.numerical_probe: Call Lasso(alpha=0.1).fit([[0],[0],[0]],[0,0,0]) and record whether a ConvergenceWarning is emitted; the answer should differ between the two revisions. Do not check coefficient values, which are zero on both.
risks: The transition depends on the ConvergenceWarning being escalated to an error by the test run. If the project's pytest configuration ignores ConvergenceWarning globally, test_lasso_zero will pass on both revisions and will not detect the bug. The -W error::sklearn.exceptions.ConvergenceWarning flag is added to force the transition; verify it takes effect.

The w_max == 0 branch and the n_iter == max_iter - 1 forced check end iteration regardless of the comparison. For zero data w_max stays 0, so the gap check is the decisive comparison, but this reasoning comes from the evidence and has not been run.

The exact equality case is what flips the outcome. Only zero data gives exact 0.0 == 0.0 without floating-point noise. Nonzero reproductions can land on either side of tol by rounding, so they are not robust transitions.

No initialisation, iteration count, dtype or magnitude regime is given in the evidence, so a generic random-data reproduction may not hit the equality and could fail to transition. Those values must be taken from the original report, not inferred.

The reproducing diff touches many tests unrelated to this stopping-criterion change, including sparse-container and column-vector warning filters. Only the coordinate-descent tests tied to the tolerance check are relevant to the transition.
The build requires a compiled Cython extension. A stale build from the wrong revision will give a false result, so rebuild after switching commits.

No platform or architecture-specific behaviour is evidenced. A fix that only shows under a specific sanitiser or BLAS backend is not claimed here, so the transition is expected on a standard Linux x86_64 build.

oracle.why: The gap and tolerance are both exactly 0.0 for zero data, so the comparison is an exact equality check with no numerical tolerance involved.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 3c74809cb3ef, Lasso.fit on all-zero data hits 0.0 < 0.0 (false), so the solver does not stop at the gap check and emits a ConvergenceWarning; with that warning escalated to an error, test_lasso_zero fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, 0.0 <= 0.0 is true, the solver stops at the first gap check, no ConvergenceWarning is emitted, and test_lasso_zero passes.
